 Northeast Monsoon to begin Oct 27, bringing 3 to 5 episodes of heavy rain 
 By Kalbana Perimbanayagam 
 October 23, 2026 @ 5:35pm 
 Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) says the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon is expected to begin on Oct 27, bringing three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain between November and January. – NSTP file pic
 HUJANSHAH ALAM 27 NOVEMBER 2025. Kelihatan awan gelap serta hujan mula turun disekitar Stadium Shah Alam. MET Malaysia telah mengemas kini Amaran Ribut Tropika, Amaran Angin Kencang dan Laut Bergelora bagi negeri Kedah, Pulau Pinang, Perak, Pahang, Selangor, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur, Wilayah Persekutuan Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka dan Johor berkuatkuasa dari 27-29 November 2025. STR/ AZIAH AZMEE
 KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon is expected to begin on Oct 27, bringing three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain between November and January that could trigger floods in low-lying areas and riverine communities.
 Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the monsoon would last until March next year and be characterised by persistent northeast winds.
 He said strong winds could also cause rough seas and raise sea levels, particularly in the South China Sea.
 Rainfall is expected to ease during the final phase, from January to March, particularly in the northern peninsula and Sabah.
 "This condition will result in hot and dry weather and could lead to more extreme heatwaves due to the influence of the very strong (Super) El Niño phenomenon currently occurring," he said in a statement today.
 Hisham advised the public to remain vigilant and monitor weather forecasts and warnings issued by MetMalaysia throughout the monsoon.
 Updates are available on MetMalaysia's website, through the myCuaca mobile application and its official social media platforms, or via its hotline at 1-300-22-1638.
